page: Google Cloud Platform a3-ultragpu-8g-nolssd is an accelerator-optimized server configured with eight NVIDIA H200 GPUs from the Hopper family, providing a total of 1123 GB of VRAM. The host system is powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor with 224 dedicated vCPUs (112 physical cores) operating at 2.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. System memory totals 2952.0 GB, yielding approximately 13.18 GB of RAM per core. A key architectural tradeoff of this specific configuration is the complete absence of local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier multi-core CPU and memory performance. The server achieved a multi-core stress-ng score of 180184.5 and a PassMark CPU score of 125594.41, both placing in the top 10% tier. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with cached small-block read speeds reaching 13946.39 GB/sec and large-block uncached write speeds at 188.23 GB/sec. Single-core performance remains in the average tier, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 1959.0. In LLM text generation benchmarks, the system achieved 32.58 tokens per second on a medium 7B model and 2.96 tokens per second on a large 70B model.

Given the high density of eight NVIDIA H200 GPUs and nearly 3 TB of system memory, this server represents a premium hardware class designed for extreme computational workloads. The lack of local SSD storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which is a critical architectural consideration for data-intensive pipelines. This configuration is highly suited for large-scale deep learning, LLM training and inference, advanced ray tracing, and massive parallel compute tasks where GPU acceleration and high memory capacity are required.
